why: Different conclusions. B (Milnor's sentence): on an abstract smooth manifold with g⁻¹[a,b] compact and all critical points there non-degenerate of index ≥ λ₀, there is a relative CW complex (Y, D) without cells of dimension < λ₀, D ≃ g⁻¹(−∞,a], Y ≃ g⁻¹(−∞,b] compatibly. A (universes 0; lemma_D): for f = F|N on a slice submanifold, F smooth on V, N^{a₀} compact, a a REGULAR value, critical points with a < f ≤ a₀ non-degenerate of index ≥ λ₀, b < a₀: N^a pushes maps from any compact P ⊆ ℝ^{<λ₀} out of N^b (homotopy rel the preimage of N^a) — the consequence Milnor draws next ('since r < λ₀, h is homotopic into g⁻¹(−∞,2δ]'). A ⇒ B fails genuinely (a compression property gives no CW model; that needs Theorems 3.1/3.2 assembled into a relative CW complex, not in A; setting). B ⇒ A fails genuinely (cellular approximation / push-off for arbitrary compact P rel an arbitrary closed subset, transport along the compatible homotopy equivalences; setting; B does not need a regular or N^{a₀} compact but A's F is ambient). exists_gap_of_finite is a trivial real-analysis lemma (true outright).
embedded_special_case_note: B is about smooth (not Riemannian) manifolds; B at M = Bridge.Sub hN is a special case, but even there the conclusions are of different kinds (CW model vs compression of maps from compact P ⊆ ℝ^{<λ₀}); bridging them is cellular approximation, not dictionary glue. Not attempted.
